notes: Pure algorithm property of `fetchAvailableVersions`'s walk loop (lines 93-107), independent of any real API response: it stops after 20 candidates are *tried* (`tried += 1` at line 99, checked against `maxCandidates = 20` at line 94) regardless of how few results have been collected -- the two guard conditions (`tried < maxCandidates`, `results.count < limit`) are ANDed, so hitting either one ends the walk. This is the mechanism the real fallback described in the function's own doc comment (lines 64-68, "if a high version number has no STABLE builds, the selector automatically falls back to the next lower version") relies on -- it only works because 20 is normally far more than enough candidates to reach a real stable version; a version list where the top 20 entries are all unreleased/broken would exhaust the cap and return nothing rather than walking further down. `paper-best-build-selection-stable-wins-beta-fallback-when-absent` exercises the shape of a single call inside this loop; this case exercises the loop's own termination rule.
